name: XOR
description: XOR returns TRUE when an odd number of its logical arguments are TRUE, and FALSE otherwise. It is the logical exclusive OR.
tldr: Returns TRUE when an odd number of arguments are TRUE.

parameters.name: logical1
parameters.description: The first condition or logical value to test.

parameters.name: logical2
parameters.description: Additional conditions or logical values to test (optional).

basicExample.explanation: One of the two arguments is TRUE (an odd count), so XOR returns TRUE.

advancedExamples.title: Two true is false
advancedExamples.explanation: Two TRUE values are an even count, so XOR returns FALSE.

advancedExamples.title: Three inputs
advancedExamples.scenario: Cells A1:A3 are TRUE, FALSE, TRUE
advancedExamples.explanation: Two of the three are TRUE (even), so the result is FALSE.

howItWorks: XOR evaluates each argument as TRUE or FALSE (non-zero numbers count as TRUE), counts how many are TRUE, and returns TRUE when that count is odd and FALSE when even.

howToSteps.name: List conditions
howToSteps.text: Provide the logical tests or values.

limitations: Available only in Excel 2013 and later.
With exactly two arguments it behaves as classic XOR; with more it is true for any odd number of TRUEs, not 'exactly one'.

commonErrors.cause: An argument is text that is not a valid logical value.
commonErrors.fix: Pass real conditions or TRUE/FALSE constants.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: XOR is supported in Google Sheets with the same syntax and odd-count behavior.

faq.question: Does XOR mean 'exactly one'?
faq.answer: Only with two arguments; with more it returns TRUE for any odd number of TRUEs.

faq.question: How is XOR different from OR?
faq.answer: OR is TRUE if any argument is true; XOR is TRUE only for an odd number of true arguments.
